title: Update the pull request
concept: Push more commits to the same branch; the PR updates itself

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Now actually do what Priya asked. Add the opening hours to food.html.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: You do **not** make a new pull request. You add a commit to the same branch.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Commit it and push. Watch the pull request pick up the new commit on its own.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Then tell Priya it is ready for another look.

hub.body: Good start. One change needed before I can approve.

comments.body: Can you add the opening hours here?

items.text: Add the opening hours to food.html and commit
Push to the same branch so the pull request updates
Tell Priya it is ready for another look

hints: Edit the file, commit, push to the branch you are already on. No new pull request.
After pushing, add a comment on the pull request so the reviewer knows to look again.
Edit food.html to add "Open 11am to 9pm", then `git add food.html`, `git commit -m "Add opening hours"`, `git push`, then comment on the pull request in the website panel.
recap: Pushing more commits to the same branch updates the open pull request. You never need a second pull request for review fixes.

predict.question: You pushed a new commit to food-stalls. What happens to pull request #1?

choices.text: It picks up the new commit automatically
It stays frozen and you need a new pull request

predict.explanation: A pull request points at a branch, not at a fixed snapshot. Whatever is on the branch is what it shows.
